foodCost.factorsSubtitle: These factors differ in every restaurant, so food cost differs too.
foodCost.factor1Content: What you pay for ingredients. This is in your hands: check the market, ask several suppliers for prices, find the same quality for less. Use what was bought first, first. Compare prices every week.
foodCost.factor2Content: Never set a price without a recipe and a cost calculation. First work out food cost, then set the price from your target percentage. Pricing “like the place next door” is the biggest mistake. The right way: portion cost ÷ target food cost % = selling price.
foodCost.factor3Content: The same menu can give a different food cost in two months — it depends on what sells more. Push the dishes that earn most; fix the price of low earners or take them off the menu. The “Menu matrix” tool helps with this.
foodCost.factor4Content: Following recipes, staff meals, spoiled stock, free treats, cash shortages — all must be controlled. Use what was bought first, first. Meat is the most expensive loss — start there. Count stock weekly and compare with what you expected.

staffRetention.preShiftTitle: Why does a 10-minute meeting before the shift work?
staffRetention.preShiftBody: Ten minutes with the team before every shift cuts surprises and stress: special bookings, the dish of the day and yesterday’s problem reach everyone the same way. It is one of the cheapest staff tools there is.
staffRetention.dkAdviceBody: If the share of staff leaving grows year after year, the cause is usually the way things are run, not pay. Until hiring, a new hire’s first weeks, the pre-shift meeting and a last talk with leavers are written down as rules, a stable team is hard to build.

staffRetention.strategy2: Plan a new hire’s first 2 weeks: an experienced colleague as a guide and training in several roles.
staffRetention.strategy3: Beyond pay: staff meals, a flexible shift schedule and a way to thank people for good work.
staffRetention.strategy4: Hold a 10-minute team meeting before every shift.
staffRetention.strategy5: Announce how tips are split, in writing and open to everyone.
staffRetention.strategy6: Show the steps for promotion and pay in advance.

deliveryCalc.deliveryMathBody: Three large platforms operate in Baku: Wolt, Bolt Food and Yango. The rate they charge restaurants is not published as an open price list — it depends on the contract, promotions and dish type. So you take the rate from your own contract and enter it; the 30% and 10% on the cards are only examples.
deliveryCalc.tip1: Build a separate delivery menu: drop dishes that go cold or get crushed on the way.
deliveryCalc.tip2: Price delivery a little above the dine-in menu (for example 10% — work it out from your commission).
deliveryCalc.tip3: Sets (dish + drink + dessert) raise the average order value.
deliveryCalc.tip4: Cut packaging down to a few standard sizes and buy in bulk.
deliveryCalc.tip5: In a promotion, work out separately who pays for the discount — you or the platform.
deliveryCalc.tip6: Track each platform’s income and costs apart from the main till.
deliveryCalc.tip7: Over time, move regular customers to your own channel: website, WhatsApp, phone.
deliveryCalc.contractQ1: Is the commission fixed, or does it change with promotions and dish type?
deliveryCalc.contractQ2: Which part of a promotion discount does the restaurant pay?
deliveryCalc.contractQ3: On which dates is money paid out, and when is the commission deducted?
deliveryCalc.contractQ4: Is there a penalty for leaving the contract, and how many days’ notice is needed?
deliveryCalc.contractQ5: Can delivery menu prices differ from dine-in prices?
deliveryCalc.contractQ6: Are advertising, promotion and visibility services charged separately?
deliveryCalc.contractQ7: Who is responsible for refunds and complaints?
deliveryCalc.dkAdviceBody: Do not treat delivery as “extra sales” — run the numbers on it as a separate business. If price, discounts and packaging are not in one table, even high sales can leave little profit.

aqtaChecklist.aqtaCardDesc: AQTA is the Azerbaijan Food Safety Agency. It checks food safety, hygiene and whether you can show with documents where your food came from. Cleanliness alone is not enough: the rules must be followed and written down every day. AQTA registration applications are submitted via ASAN/KOBİA. There is no state fee; the application is free.

aqtaChecklist.crossContamDesc: When germs from raw meat reach ready food, it can cause food poisoning. The riskiest trio: one cutting board, one pair of gloves and the wrong order in the fridge. Coloured boards help prevent this:
aqtaChecklist.dkAdviceDesc: An AQTA problem is usually not a "cleanliness problem" but a "management rhythm problem". If there is no log, no responsible person and no daily monitoring hour, the penalty risk increases.

aqtaChecklist.storage_item4_text: Food is stored off the floor

aqtaChecklist.storage_item5_text: Older stock is at the front, use-by dates are labelled
aqtaChecklist.storage_item5_detail: «First in, first out» (FIFO): older products at the front, nothing past its date.
aqtaChecklist.hygiene_subtitle: Team behavior, hairnet, medical certificate and handwashing
aqtaChecklist.hygiene_item1_text: All staff have current medical certificates
aqtaChecklist.hygiene_item2_text: Work attire is clean and meets standards
aqtaChecklist.hygiene_item2_detail: Kitchen team wears light-colored uniform and hairnet.
aqtaChecklist.hygiene_item3_detail: Soap, sanitizer and dryer are always fully stocked.
aqtaChecklist.hygiene_item4_text: Nail, accessory and smoking rules are enforced
aqtaChecklist.hygiene_item4_detail: Rings, bracelets and no-smoking rule in kitchen are not violated.
aqtaChecklist.kitchen_subtitle: Surfaces, boards, waste and pest control
aqtaChecklist.kitchen_item1_text: Work surfaces and knives are cleaned after each use
aqtaChecklist.kitchen_item1_detail: Cleaning and disinfection are separate processes, both applied.
aqtaChecklist.kitchen_item2_detail: Separate boards designated for raw meat, poultry, fish and vegetables.
aqtaChecklist.kitchen_item3_text: Waste bins have lids and are pedal-operated
aqtaChecklist.kitchen_item3_detail: No overflow, odors or open waste areas.
aqtaChecklist.kitchen_item4_detail: Weekly inspection and professional pest control plan is maintained.
aqtaChecklist.water_subtitle: Drinking water, ice machine and safe service
aqtaChecklist.water_item1_detail: Filter, service and maintenance timing are monitored.
aqtaChecklist.water_item2_detail: Ice is handled with tongs or a scoop, not by hand.
aqtaChecklist.water_item3_text: Containers in contact with water are separated
aqtaChecklist.water_item3_detail: Ice container, water container and dishwasher drain are not mixed.
aqtaChecklist.prep_subtitle: Cooking temperature, holding limit and reheating
aqtaChecklist.prep_item1_text: Chicken reaches minimum internal temperature of 74°C
aqtaChecklist.prep_item1_detail: Checked with a thermometer, not judged by appearance.
aqtaChecklist.prep_item2_text: Ready food stays at room temperature no longer than 2 hours
aqtaChecklist.prep_item2_detail: After 2 hours it is refrigerated or discarded.
aqtaChecklist.prep_item3_detail: The same safety boundary is maintained for repeated service.
aqtaChecklist.prep_item4_text: Same gloves are not used across different product groups
aqtaChecklist.prep_item4_detail: Cross-contamination rules are known by the team.
aqtaChecklist.docs_subtitle: AQTA registration, logs and documents showing where products come from
aqtaChecklist.docs_item1_detail: AQTA registration applications are submitted via ASAN/KOBİA. There is no state fee — registration is free of charge.
aqtaChecklist.docs_item2_text: Temperature and hygiene log is filled in
aqtaChecklist.docs_item2_detail: Daily entries are never left blank.
aqtaChecklist.docs_item3_text: Invoices and product source documents are archived
aqtaChecklist.docs_item3_detail: During an inspection you can show with documents where each product came from.
aqtaChecklist.docs_item4_text: Medical certificate dates are tracked in a separate table
aqtaChecklist.docs_item4_detail: Renewal reminders are given before expiry.
aqtaChecklist.hall_subtitle: Toilet, ventilation and overall sanitation appearance
aqtaChecklist.hall_item1_text: Toilet is clean and fully equipped
aqtaChecklist.hall_item1_detail: Soap, dryer and running water are available.
aqtaChecklist.hall_item2_text: Kitchen odors do not reach the dining area
aqtaChecklist.hall_item2_detail: Ventilation flow and filter cleanliness are monitored.
aqtaChecklist.hall_item3_text: Floor, walls and ceiling are sanitation-compliant
aqtaChecklist.hall_item3_detail: No grease, mold or visible grime on surfaces.
aqtaChecklist.allergen_subtitle: Menu information and clear guest warnings
aqtaChecklist.allergen_item1_text: Main allergens are noted on the menu
aqtaChecklist.allergen_item1_detail: Milk, gluten, eggs, nuts etc. are clearly indicated.
aqtaChecklist.allergen_item2_detail: Service staff have a short response script.
aqtaChecklist.allergen_item3_text: A separate preparation rule exists for allergens
aqtaChecklist.allergen_item3_detail: Board, knife and surface separation is known.
aqtaChecklist.daily_item1: Record refrigerator and freezer temperatures in the log.
aqtaChecklist.daily_item3: Check that older stock is at the front and check the use-by dates.
aqtaChecklist.daily_item4: Check that handwashing stations have soap and dryer.
aqtaChecklist.daily_item5: Monitor work attire, hairnet and glove compliance.
aqtaChecklist.weekly_item1: Fully clean the inside of refrigerators.
aqtaChecklist.weekly_item2: Check corners and backs of shelves for pest risk.
aqtaChecklist.weekly_item3: Inspect cutting boards for cracks and wear.
aqtaChecklist.weekly_item4: Deep clean ventilation filters and toilet hygiene.
aqtaChecklist.monthly_item2: Archive invoices and product source documents.
aqtaChecklist.monthly_item3: Complete the equipment technical inspection list.
aqtaChecklist.monthly_item4: Give the team a 15-minute hygiene refresher.
aqtaChecklist.monthly_item5: Schedule professional pest control or inspection service.
aqtaChecklist.fine4: Raw and ready-to-eat food stored together
aqtaChecklist.fine9: Non-compliant work attire and hairnet rule

insaatChecklist.pageTitle: From construction to opening: work list
insaatChecklist.pageDesc: A 62-item work plan: from wiring to fire safety (FHN), from the trial opening to the official opening — every step in order.
insaatChecklist.budgetSubtitle: Example: rough split for a 50–80 m², 30–40 seat restaurant. The figures are only a guide — check them against your builders’ quotes.
insaatChecklist.budgetTotalNote: Sum of the rows above: from – to.
insaatChecklist.dkAdviceSubtitle: Construction is where the most expensive mistakes happen
insaatChecklist.dkAdviceDesc: In construction, a cheap contractor, an unplanned phase and an unwritten agreement directly translate into time and money loss. The most critical trio: 3-phase electrical, gas and chimney. Don't tear down walls before these are resolved.
insaatChecklist.mistake1: Starting without checking the 3-phase power supply and then paying thousands of manats extra.
insaatChecklist.mistake2: Choosing a cheap contractor and having to redo water and electrical lines.
insaatChecklist.mistake3: Drawing the kitchen plan without a chef and not being able to fit the equipment later.
insaatChecklist.mistake4: Not setting aside a contingency fund and running into cash flow problems at the final stage.
insaatChecklist.ocaqDesc: If you want to see in one panel which stage you are at, how the contractors are doing and how far the budget has moved, use OCAQ Panel.
insaatChecklist.related3Title: Break-even point (the sales level with no loss)
insaatChecklist.phase_prep_subtitle: Technical and legal foundation before construction begins
insaatChecklist.phase_prep_item1_detail: Do not start the project without Azərişıq technical inspection.
insaatChecklist.phase_prep_item2_detail: If a new line is needed, include it in the budget upfront.
insaatChecklist.phase_prep_item3_detail: Confirm compatibility with the kitchen plan.
insaatChecklist.phase_prep_item4_detail: Assess complaint and municipality risk in advance.
insaatChecklist.phase_prep_item5_detail: Minimum 3 meters is comfortable for suspended ceiling and ventilation.
insaatChecklist.phase_prep_item6_detail: Ensure no tax or DSMF debt causes problems later.
insaatChecklist.phase_prep_item7_detail: Kitchen, hall, storage and toilet planned according to flow.
insaatChecklist.phase_prep_item8_detail: Do not start without setting aside a buffer for hidden costs.
insaatChecklist.phase_prep_item10_detail: Time, price, materials and delay clauses must be in the document.
insaatChecklist.phase_prep_item11_detail: Food safety side should proceed in parallel.
insaatChecklist.phase_prep_item12_detail: Do not leave fire safety plan to the last day.
insaatChecklist.phase_rough_item1_detail: Old walls, floor and suspended ceiling cleared.
insaatChecklist.phase_rough_item2_detail: Kitchen, hall, storage and toilet properly separated.
insaatChecklist.phase_rough_item3_detail: Sink, dishwasher and cleaning points are ready.
insaatChecklist.phase_rough_item5_detail: Separate lines allocated for kitchen, hall and lighting.
insaatChecklist.phase_rough_item7_detail: Kitchen and hall zones are separated.
insaatChecklist.phase_rough_item8_detail: Filter and fire protection not forgotten.
insaatChecklist.phase_rough_item10_detail: Compatible with lighting and ventilation points.
insaatChecklist.phase_finish_item1_detail: Concept colors match the design decision.
insaatChecklist.phase_finish_item2_detail: Separate materials for hall and kitchen.
insaatChecklist.phase_finish_item4_detail: Consider different scenarios for day and evening.
insaatChecklist.phase_finish_item5_detail: Hall, storage and kitchen temperatures tracked separately.
insaatChecklist.phase_finish_item6_detail: Customer and staff zones are separate.
insaatChecklist.phase_finish_item7_text: Bar and cashier area is ready
insaatChecklist.phase_finish_item11_detail: Visual moments that make guests want to take photos created.
insaatChecklist.phase_equipment_subtitle: The working brain of the kitchen
insaatChecklist.phase_equipment_item4_detail: Water and drainage flow is problem-free.
insaatChecklist.phase_equipment_item5_detail: Correct height selected for hygiene and workflow.
insaatChecklist.phase_equipment_item7_detail: A separate reliable line for POS.
insaatChecklist.phase_equipment_item8_detail: Kitchen, cashier and entrance minimally monitored.
insaatChecklist.phase_opening_subtitle: Construction done, now a risk-free start
insaatChecklist.phase_opening_item1_detail: Hygiene and documentation is ready for opening.
insaatChecklist.phase_opening_item2_detail: Fire equipment and exit plan confirmed.
insaatChecklist.phase_opening_item4_detail: Menu, POS, service and hygiene practiced together.
insaatChecklist.phase_opening_item5_detail: Run a real test service with friends and acquaintances.
insaatChecklist.phase_opening_item6_detail: Food cost and sales language are finalized.
insaatChecklist.phase_opening_item7_detail: Marketing, guest list and social media plan is ready.
insaatChecklist.phase_design_subtitle: When the architect's sketch arrives — before construction
insaatChecklist.phase_design_item1_detail: The menu defines the equipment, and the equipment defines electricity, water and gas needs. Don't commission a floor plan without this document.
insaatChecklist.phase_design_item2_detail: Photograph the facade from across the street by day and by night: does the venue stand out, is the entrance clear, can you see inside?
insaatChecklist.phase_design_item3_detail: Draw the route from the door to the table, till, restroom and exit on the plan. Guests should find it without signs.
insaatChecklist.phase_design_item4_text: Product flow: from receiving to plate
insaatChecklist.phase_design_item4_detail: Receiving → inspection → storage → prep → cooking → pass → service. The flow must not double back or cross the guest entrance.
insaatChecklist.phase_design_item5_detail: Dirty dishes enter on one side, clean ones leave on the other. The dishwashing area runs in one direction.
insaatChecklist.phase_design_item6_text: Movement lines on the sketch («spaghetti diagram»)
insaatChecklist.phase_design_item6_detail: Trace the route of one cook, one server and one guest on the architect's sketch. If the lines cross, don't move on to construction drawings.
insaatChecklist.phase_design_item7_detail: How many orders per hour can the kitchen, bar, pass and dishwashing handle at peak? The weakest point sets the speed of the whole restaurant.
insaatChecklist.phase_design_item8_detail: Separate spots for solo guests, couples, groups, families and business meetings. Identical four-tops leave the room half empty.
insaatChecklist.phase_design_item9_detail: A step-free wheelchair route from the entrance to the table and restroom, and a clear, marked evacuation route — in the plan from day one.
insaatChecklist.phase_design_item10_text: Timings to measure at the trial opening
insaatChecklist.phase_design_item10_detail: Record 10 timings: order to table, bill to payment, table reset. Without numbers, a trial opening is just a rehearsal.

finance_cash_q1.text: Is daily cash closing reconciled between POS/Z-report and actual cash/card totals?
finance_cash_q1.tooltip: If end-of-day gaps are not visible, losses, errors and cancellations escape control.

finance_cash_q2.text: Is every sale closed with a fiscal receipt and are discounts, cancellations and refunds tracked separately?
finance_cash_q2.tooltip: Fiscal discipline keeps a real sales trail and strengthens internal control.

finance_cash_q3.text: Does the monthly expense report show sales, food, labor, rent, utilities, marketing and net profit together?
finance_cash_q3.tooltip: Separate notes are not enough for decisions; the owner needs one-page visibility.

finance_cash_q4.text: Is core cost (food plus staff as a share of sales) tracked every month, and is actual food cost compared with recipe cost?
finance_cash_q4.tooltip: Food and labor are the main margin signal. A small drift can create a large annual loss.

finance_cash_q5.text: Are the weekly top-10 sold products known and is each product margin calculated?
finance_cash_q5.tooltip: A high-selling item with weak margin is a hidden loss source on the menu.

operations_kitchen_q1.text: Are HACCP and food safety practices part of daily kitchen operations?
operations_kitchen_q1.tooltip: The procedure must work during prep and service, not only on paper.

operations_kitchen_q2.text: Is inventory counted periodically and compared with system stock?
operations_kitchen_q2.tooltip: Without counts, theft, waste and purchasing errors stay invisible.

operations_kitchen_q3.text: Are waste and loss recorded in a separate log?
operations_kitchen_q3.tooltip: If discarded product is not explained, rising food cost becomes hard to diagnose.

operations_kitchen_q4.text: Do FIFO and date labels work across all prep and storage areas?
operations_kitchen_q4.tooltip: Undated product is a quality, compliance and cost risk.

operations_kitchen_q5.text: Is the gap between actual food cost and theoretical recipe food cost tracked?
operations_kitchen_q5.tooltip: Portion drift, waste and price changes show up in this gap.

staff_service_q1.text: Is there written onboarding material and a checklist for new staff?
staff_service_q1.tooltip: When training stays verbal, service standards change from shift to shift.

staff_service_q2.text: Is the service protocol applied consistently by the team?
staff_service_q2.tooltip: Greeting, order taking, complaint handling and payment should follow the same rhythm.

staff_service_q3.text: Does the team know specific products and phrases for upselling?
staff_service_q3.tooltip: Upselling is a system for proposing higher-margin items, not random pressure.

staff_service_q4.text: Are shifts planned around peak and quiet hours?
staff_service_q4.tooltip: Wrong shifts damage both service speed and labor percentage.

staff_service_q5.text: Is staff turnover and exit reason tracked monthly?
staff_service_q5.tooltip: Repeated exit reasons are an early warning signal for management.

customer_experience_q1.text: Are Google and social reviews monitored weekly?
customer_experience_q1.tooltip: Review flow is the real market mirror for the restaurant.

customer_experience_q2.text: Is there a process for complaint response, correction and follow-up?
customer_experience_q2.tooltip: A complaint is not just a reply; it is a process to prevent repeated errors.

customer_experience_q3.text: Is there a loyalty or return-visit mechanism in use?
customer_experience_q3.tooltip: New customers are expensive; returning customers protect margin.

customer_experience_q4.text: Are table turnover and waiting time tracked?
customer_experience_q4.tooltip: During peak hours, table turnover directly changes sales capacity.

customer_experience_q5.text: Is repeat customer percentage and reason for return known?

digital_presence_q2.text: Is the online order or reservation process clear?
digital_presence_q2.tooltip: Extra steps in the customer journey create sales loss.

digital_presence_q3.text: Are mobile menu, prices and photo quality comfortable for the customer?
digital_presence_q3.tooltip: Mobile viewing is one of the core restaurant selection moments.

digital_presence_q4.text: Is social activity connected to campaign and menu priorities?
digital_presence_q4.tooltip: Posting is not enough; content should support sales and reputation goals.

digital_presence_q5.text: Is campaign source tracked through promo code, UTM or channel notes?
digital_presence_q5.tooltip: If source is unknown, working channels cannot be separated from weak ones.

compliance_risk_q1.text: Are food safety registration and sanitary documents in order?
compliance_risk_q1.tooltip: Compliance should be tracked as a working checklist, without relying on memory.

compliance_risk_q2.text: Are medical checks for food-contact staff tracked?
compliance_risk_q2.tooltip: Medical monitoring reduces both compliance and customer safety risk.

compliance_risk_q3.text: If delivery exists, is the temperature regime maintained?
compliance_risk_q3.tooltip: Temperature drift during delivery is a quality and safety risk.

compliance_risk_q4.text: Are cleaning, disinfection and pest-control actions logged?
compliance_risk_q4.tooltip: A process without logs is hard to prove in audit and hard to manage internally.

compliance_risk_q5.text: Are employment contracts, insurance and safety processes in order?
compliance_risk_q5.tooltip: Team risk directly affects the restaurant legal and operational stability.

beverage_focus.fallbackFirstStep: Add one cold coffee, one homemade lemonade and one photogenic seasonal drink to a mini drink board.

sustainability_local.fallbackFirstStep: Name one local supplier or seasonal ingredient on the menu and start a daily waste note.

experience_human_touch.title: Experience and human touch

experience_human_touch.fallbackFirstStep: Give the team one personal touch rule for each table: name, signature story and a short feedback question.

explain.entryFeeDesc: This is your access to the system. Paid ONCE when the contract is signed — it "unlocks" the brand name, system and training. Not to be confused with monthly royalties.
explain.royaltyDesc: An ongoing fee for continued use of the brand and support. Usually a percentage of monthly turnover.

explain.franchiseTypesTitle: Franchise type — the "the country is mine" misconception
explain.singleUnitDesc: The right to operate in ONE location only. The most common model. Does NOT give you a region or country.
explain.areaDesc: The right to open multiple outlets in a defined area (city/district).
explain.masterDesc: Rights for an entire COUNTRY or large region; you can grant sub-franchises to others. Most expensive, most obligations.
explain.subDesc: Rights granted by the master or area franchisee — not directly from the brand.
explain.warning: Warning: "I bought a franchise, so the country is mine" is NOT TRUE. A standard single-unit franchise gives you just one location. Country rights = master franchise = separate and much higher fee + obligations.

basabas.r: Minimum monthly sales and customers needed per day
basabas.kw: break even break-even minimum sales customers branch opening cost
basabas.what: Shows how much you must sell each month to avoid a loss, how many customers you need a day and whether the money is enough for a new branch.
how: Enter monthly fixed costs — example café: rent 3,000 ₼, wages 5,000 ₼, utilities 800 ₼, other 700 ₼.
Enter variable costs (ingredients, packaging — 35% of sales in the example) and the average check (25 ₼).
Result: you need at least 14,615 ₼ of sales a month, about 20 checks a day. With current sales of 18,000 ₼ the cushion before a loss is 18.8%.

delivery-calc.d: Wolt, Bolt Food, Yango and your own courier: what is left from an order after commission.
delivery-calc.r: What you keep from an order on each platform
delivery-calc.kw: wolt bolt yango commission delivery courier
delivery-calc.what: Shows what you keep from one order after platform commission, ingredients and packaging — it helps you decide which channel is worth selling through.
how: Pick the platforms you sell on and enter the commission rate from your contract (example: Wolt 30%).
Enter the average order, ingredient share, packaging and staff cost (example: 30 ₼ order, 33% ingredients, 1.50 ₼ packaging, 3 ₼ staff).
Read the result: in the example you keep 17.10 ₼ in the dining room but 6.60 ₼ on Wolt — close the gap with price or a separate delivery menu.

addim-xerci.d: Turn the time cooks and waiters spend on empty walks into monthly wage loss.
addim-xerci.r: Monthly wages spent on empty walking (₼)
addim-xerci.kw: steps walking kitchen layout spaghetti diagram
addim-xerci.what: Shows how many manats of wages a month your cooks’ and waiters’ empty walking costs — it helps you decide whether moving equipment is worth it.
how: At peak time, watch one person for 30 minutes and draw their empty trips as lines on a paper floor plan.
Enter the staff count, empty walking per day and hourly wage (example: 3 cooks, 40 minutes a day each, 6 ₼ an hour, 26 working days).
Result: in the example 312 ₼ a month and 3,744 ₼ a year go on empty walking — move the fridge or service table closer and measure again.

menu-matrix.d: One step for every dish: keep, fix the price, promote or remove.
menu-matrix.r: For every dish: keep, fix the price, promote or remove
menu-matrix.kw: menu dish sales earnings price menu engineering
menu-matrix.what: Shows which dish to keep, where to fix the price, what to promote and what to take off the menu.
how: Enter each dish's monthly sales and what you earn on one portion (selling price − ingredient cost). Example: chicken saj — 120 portions a month, 8.50 ₼ per portion.
The tool compares every dish with the menu average: does it sell a lot (over 70% of average sales) and does it earn more than average.
You get one step per dish. Chicken saj sells a lot and earns well → «Keep»: keep the recipe and price, place it where guests see it.

qonaq-evi-roi-kalkulyatoru.d: Work out monthly profit and how long it takes to get your money back from room price, booked days and Booking/Airbnb commission.
qonaq-evi-roi-kalkulyatoru.r: Monthly profit and how many months until your money is back
qonaq-evi-roi-kalkulyatoru.kw: guesthouse income profit booking airbnb commission payback roi
qonaq-evi-roi-kalkulyatoru.what: Shows how much profit your guesthouse makes a month and how many months it takes to earn back the opening cost — helps you decide whether to change your price or the commission you pay to sites.
how: Enter the room price, number of rooms, share of booked days and the Booking/Airbnb commission. Example: a 4-room guesthouse in Shaki, 100 ₼ a night, booked 40% of the month, 15% commission.
Add monthly costs and the opening cost (renovation, furniture). Example: 1,500 ₼ a month, 20,000 ₼ to open.
The tool shows monthly profit and the payback time. In the example 70% of guests come from the sites: profit 2,796 ₼ a month, money back in about 7 months.

ota-hazirlig-testi.d: Check in 8 questions how ready your guesthouse is for booking sites like Booking and Airbnb.
ota-hazirlig-testi.kw: booking airbnb ota yandex travel guesthouse listing reservation
ota-hazirlig-testi.what: Shows whether you are ready to list on online booking sites (OTAs) such as Booking and Airbnb, and what to fix first.
how: Answer 8 questions: photos, listing, price, calendar, reviews, payment, language and direct booking.
Each answer gives 25–100 points; the tool works out the average and your weakest area.
Example: a 3-room house in Gabala — dark photos (25 points), the other 7 areas average (50 points). Average 47: «You can start on Booking.com», weakest area — photos.

whatsapp-template-paketi.d: Ready messages for guesthouses and hotels: from the first hello to an offer for a regular guest.
whatsapp-template-paketi.kw: whatsapp guest message template guesthouse hotel
whatsapp-template-paketi.what: Gives you ready messages so you can write to guests quickly and neatly — no need to write the text from scratch every time.
how: Pick the message you need: first hello, arrival day instructions, thanks for a review and more.
Press «Copy» and paste the message into WhatsApp.
Replace the parts in brackets with your details. Example: [guest name] → Elvin, [time] → 14:00.

checklist.d: Papers, premises, kitchen, menu, staff, promotion and money — 43 things to do before you open.
checklist.r: The tasks left before opening day
checklist.what: Helps you not forget anything important before opening a restaurant: what is ready and what is left, at a glance.
how: Open a section and tick what is already done. For example, you are opening a 40-seat café in Yasamal: tax ID obtained, lease signed.
On the right you see how much is done and what is left in each section: «Papers and official matters 2/8».
Split the rest by date and person. «Clear» removes every tick, «Undo» brings them back.

insaat-checklist.d: A 6-stage work plan from construction to opening, with notes and photos for each item.
insaat-checklist.what: Helps you do construction and fit-out work in the right order and catch expensive mistakes early.
how: Open a stage: «Preparation», «Rough work», «Finishing»… For example, you are turning a 70 m² unit in Nasimi into a restaurant.
Tick finished work and add a short note or photo: «3-phase power — checked by Azerishig, 12 October».
On the right you see what is left in each stage. Ticks are kept in this browser; «Clear» removes them and «Undo» works for 8 seconds.

aqta-checklist.t: Getting ready for an AQTA inspection
aqta-checklist.d: Hygiene, paperwork and food storage — check section by section before the inspector comes.
aqta-checklist.r: Which sections still carry a fine risk
aqta-checklist.what: Helps you find what could lead to a fine during an inspection by AQTA, the Azerbaijan Food Safety Agency.
how: Open a section and check your kitchen. For example, at a doner shop in Khatai, see whether the fridge stays between +2 °C and +6 °C.
Tick the items that are in order. «Items still at risk» shows how many are not ticked yet.
Put the rest into a daily, weekly and monthly schedule and name one person in charge. AQTA registration is free and goes through ASAN/KOBİA.

branding-guide.d: Name, one-sentence brand promise, guest, tone and colours — then a 12-step list.
branding-guide.r: A completed brand card and 12-step list
branding-guide.what: Helps you decide who your restaurant is and what it promises before you spend money on a logo and design.
how: Fill in the 5 fields of the brand card, or press «Load example»: «Grandma’s Kitchen — home cooking in Narimanov, lunch in 15 minutes».
Tick the steps on the 12-item list: two logo versions, 3–4 colours, menu design, staff training.
Show the finished card to your designer and staff so everyone builds the same brand. The card is kept in this browser.

otel-hazirlig-testi.d: Check in 12 questions how ready your hotel is for a star rating (AHA requirements).
otel-hazirlig-testi.r: Readiness score and a realistic star target
otel-hazirlig-testi.kw: hotel star rating aha certificate classification
otel-hazirlig-testi.what: Shows which star level your hotel is ready for and what to strengthen before applying to AHA.
how: Answer 12 questions: building, rooms, cleaning, reception, food, staff, documents and more.
Each answer gives 25–100 points; the average becomes a star target (e.g. 65–74 points — a 3-star target).
Example: a 25-room hotel in Baku with every answer at the 75-point level. Average 75: «4 stars are within reach».

personel-planlayici.d: How many staff a restaurant or café needs in each shift.
personel-planlayici.r: Staff per shift and wages as a share of sales
personel-planlayici.kw: staff shift waiter cook rota schedule
personel-planlayici.what: Shows how many staff to keep at opening, in the busiest hours and in the evening, and what share of sales that costs.
how: Enter the venue type, seats, receipts per day and opening hours. Example: a 60-seat restaurant in Narimanov, 150 receipts a day, 10:00–23:00.
The tool counts waiters, cooks and cashiers per shift from seats and receipts; Friday and weekends get more.
You see the staff count per shift and wages as a share of sales. If the share is above the norm, start with the evening shift.

metbex-istasyon.d: How many stations and staff a fast food kitchen needs.
metbex-istasyon.r: Stations, staff per shift and wages as a share of sales
metbex-istasyon.kw: fast food kitchen station burger pizza delivery staff
metbex-istasyon.what: Shows how many stations to split a fast food kitchen into and how many staff to keep in each shift.
how: Enter the venue type, number of menu items and orders per day. Example: a burger place by 28 May metro — 25 menu items, 180 orders a day.
Tick how guests order: eat in, takeaway, delivery. Every extra channel adds work for the kitchen.
The tool shows the stations (grill, fryer, assembly), staff per shift and wages as a share of sales.

staff-retention.d: Share of staff who left, the cost of replacing one person and money lost per year.
staff-retention.r: Money lost per year to staff leaving (₼)
staff-retention.what: Shows what the staff who left during the year cost you — it helps you decide how much money and time to put into keeping your team.
how: Enter your current staff count, average monthly salary and how many people left last year (example: 18 staff, 850 ₼, 12 people).
The tool works out the share of staff who left: in the example 12 ÷ 18 = 66.7%.
Replacing one person costs about 2–3 months of salary (a widely used rule of thumb): in the example about 25,500 ₼ is lost per year.
